InSight.ai

Product and company names have been changed due to an NDA.

InSight.ai helps businesses understand what happens in conversations between frontline staff and customers. A device at the register or front desk records interactions, and AI analyzes them to surface service issues and successful behaviors. Built for the US market, serving retail stores, gas stations, and clinics.

My role

Across the full product

As Senior UX/UI Designer, I worked across the full product: designing new features, improving existing workflows, building dashboards and admin panels, and designing the mobile app for iOS and Android. I also redesigned the company website. I translated evolving requirements into screen concepts and refined them through weekly reviews with the client's US team. Feedback from managers using the pilot informed ongoing improvements.

Challenge

Making complex data useful

  1. 01

    Information density

    The platform needed to present a large amount of conversation data without overwhelming users. Different roles needed different views — from managers reviewing store performance to teams in HR and Loss Prevention.

  2. 02

    Evolving requirements

    New features often started as verbal descriptions on client calls, before there was a shared understanding of how they should work. I needed to turn those discussions into concrete interfaces while maintaining consistency across a growing product.

Deep dive 01

Sharing insights beyond the platform

The client wanted users to share an event with people who had no access to the platform. Together with the client's CTO, we chose email: the recipient opens the content as an external page in the browser, with no account needed. I designed the emails and pages for a single recording, a store report grouping many recordings, and automatic alerts sent when an event matched preset conditions. Recordings could also expire.

Shared recording — summary and playback
Time-limited recording — expiry notice
Store alert — recordings grouped by issue
  1. 01

    A problem after launch

    Pilot users were flooded with emails. Staff kept discussing an issue the recipient already knew about, like a broken pump, and every new mention triggered another alert.

  2. 02

    Decision: Snooze, without adding noise

    I explored several placements and durations and kept it compact, in the platform's existing style. The dialog offers 24 hours, 72 hours or 1 week and makes clear it only affects your own alerts. While Snooze is on, a banner at the top of the page shows when it ends, because it applies to the whole screen, not just the summary.

  3. 03

    Closing the loop

    Recipients can rate the AI's issue tag and report what they did about the alert: forwarded it to store staff, contacted the facility manager, or something else.

Snooze dialog — duration, own alerts only
Snoozed state — page-level banner with Unsnooze
Feedback — what action did you take?

The compact layout left room for one more element: a banner inviting recipients to sign up for the platform. Every shared email reached people outside the product, so it doubled as an acquisition channel.

Deep dive 02

Making device setup easier to follow

Store managers installed the recording device wherever it was convenient. Often that meant poor audio, and the AI transcribed conversations incorrectly, so setup quality affected every insight the platform produced.

  1. 01

    Everything in one place

    With the team, we built the setup guide into the mobile app, so managers follow each step on their phone while connecting and placing the device.

  2. 02

    Illustrations drawn for this device

    I drew every illustration myself as vector outline art. No stock image shows this device, this mic or this mount, and custom art kept the platform's visual style.

  3. 03

    The hardest step: mic placement

    Mic position decides audio quality, so it got a detailed illustrated instruction. The photo report asks for a close-up (1 foot on either side) and a wide shot (10–15 feet), and users must confirm both before they can continue.

More screens

Dashboards and admin panels

Dashboards and admin panels for six roles: Admin, District Manager, Store Manager, HR, Loss Prevention and a Super Admin for the client. Filters let each role narrow the data to what they need to review.

Outcome

A consistent product across every surface

The work established a consistent design language across the website, web platform, dashboards, admin panels, and mobile app. As the platform evolved, managers also reported spending less time reviewing data, feedback that reached us through the client during weekly reviews. Time savings and financial impact were not quantitatively measured. With the product still in pilot, these are early results: fewer setup support requests, the first demo requests from shared emails, and qualitative feedback from managers.

"Working with the team was wonderful. They are a great cultural fit for us, plus things are always done on time. Highly recommend to anyone needing design or development work done!" — Client, name withheld under NDA
